title: AEP Texas lineworker honored for helping save five in Laredo plane crash
summary: For AEP Texas Line Crew Leader Fred Bouvier, serving others extends beyond restoring power.
body_text: For AEP Texas Line Crew Leader Fred Bouvier, serving others extends beyond restoring power. Bouvier was among five people honored by the Laredo Police Department for helping rescue passengers from a plane crash in Laredo. City leaders, first responders, elected officials and community members gathered during a ceremony recognizing the group for their actions that helped save five lives. "That night, I was on shift duty," Bouvier said. "As I pulled out slowly, I came across what I realized was a plane. You never expect to see a plane." After arriving, Bouvier joined a police officer and other Good Samaritans working to reach passengers trapped inside the aircraft. Following the officer's instructions, Bouvier retrieved a fire extinguisher and tools from his truck before helping contain flames around the wing. As flames subsided, the aircraft door opened slightly from the inside. Because of his height – standing 6 feet, 3 inches tall – Bouvier helped hold the door open while passengers escaped. After the five survivors escaped, Bouvier used supplies from his truck to help care for them. For Bouvier, the rescue shows the same commitment to service that defines lineworkers across AEP Texas. "In our line of work, it's always important to help people," he said. "AEP employees have gone into burning homes and helped people escape fires." He also credited the company's safety culture for preparing employees to respond during emergencies. Despite the recognition, Bouvier remains humble about his role. "I don't really feel like a hero," he said. "I'm very grateful to be recognized. Maybe it just hasn't fully hit me yet, but I'm thankful for the recognition and thankful that I'm here today to share my story."

title: Legacy Meets Innovation: Kennametal Introduces New Products
summary: We are celebrating new cutting-edge solutions across several platforms including TopSwiss™ MBS for turning, while reflecting on our journey of continuous improvement. Join us!
body_text: Fall is a great time to celebrate the change of seasons and embrace new beginnings. In that spirit, we are celebrating by launching new cutting-edge solutions across several platforms including TopSwiss™ MBS (Mirco Boring Solid) for small parts turning, while reflecting on our journey of continuous improvement. Since 1938, Kennametal has been a leader in innovation. And it all began when McKenna Metals that was founded by metallurgist Philip M. McKenna, who after years of research created revolutionary tungsten-titanium carbide alloy cutting tools specifically for working with steel. As the company evolved, in 1943 McKenna Metals became Kennametal Inc.—a recognized leader in metalworking serving customers across continents and industries including transportation, construction, aerospace and defense, machining and cutting, energy, and general engineering. “When I joined the company, we were primarily a turning company. We developed and manufactured KC850, a cobalt enrichment grade that changed the industry. It was used everywhere, on every material. It put Kennametal on the forefront,” said Scott Etling, Vice President of Global Product Management. Having a reputation for building innovative solutions for customers' most challenging applications, Kennametal came out with newer grades called KC9110 and KC9125. Both grades utilizing cobalt enrichment, but a shift was happening in the industry. Companies started to focus on developing advanced coatings, including Kennametal.

title: Stop Losing Top Devs-Make API Docs Hyper-Personal
summary: Get expert insights on hyper-personalizing API knowledge to deliver user-aware content, elevate the developer experience, and improve retention rates.
body_text: Think about how much more efficient your development team could be if documentation dynamically adjusted to their individual needs. A hyper-personalized API documentation repository delivers technical knowledge that feels as though it were written exclusively for the user accessing the portal. A resource of this kind factors in each member’s behavior, skill level, and specific work context. So, it must be sufficiently personalized to remain relevant for everyone, while not being so overly customized that it becomes difficult to navigate. This leads to a happier, more productive team, quicker onboarding of new hires, and higher API adoption across the organization. In this article, we’ll discuss effective strategies, must-have tools, and practical tips to hyper-personalize API knowledge delivery, enhance the developer experience, and strengthen team retention. Understanding Hyper-Personalization in API Docs # What Is Hyper-Personalization and How Exactly Does It Apply to API Documentation? # Hyper-personalization is aimed at delivering ultra-contextualized experiences to every unique user. In other words, every aspect of the API knowledge base—from content to navigation paths—is dynamically individualized to fit the specific roles, behaviors, preferences, and other unique characteristics of each developer on your team . A hyper-personalized documentation system differs from basic customization in that it continuously learns from and adapts to developer interactions. Since it’s user-aware, it actively studies their practices, habits, and usage patterns to understand each developer’s workflow. It observes how they navigate through documentation sections, which paths they frequently follow, and what tech stack they’re using. All this intelligence, alongside advanced filtering and smart algorithms, helps provide team members with highly granular documentation exactly when needed and optimized for their specific context, learning style, and particular development practices. How Does Hyper-Personalized API Documentation Benefit Your Dev Team? # Today’s most forward-thinking industry figures are using hyper-personalization for everything from employee onboarding to retention to career development. This same approach is now being applied within technical fields. In the context of API documentation, hyper-personalization offers (at least!) three core benefits. First, it improves developer satisfaction by surfacing pertinent knowledge materials. These materials correspond to each specialist’s use cases, seniority levels, and API interactions. Such resources save them from sorting through long-winded, generic explanations, lessen the frustration of switching between different environments, and enhance engagement with API capabilities. Second, the onboarding process for new developers is expedited through extra-customized learning paths that are designed to align with the separate objectives of each developer profile. Their documentation portal intelligently curates role-specific resources and offers on-the-spot situational guidance alongside interactive support that helps teammates experiment with API features within a controlled environment. Third, hyper-personalized documentation drives broader API adoption throughout the entire organization. When team members receive clear, exhaustive, and illustrative explanations of API capabilities and their practical applications, they’re more likely to integrate the API into their day-to-day workflows. This may also encourage technical staff to come up with new and innovative uses for the API. Hyper-Personalizing API Docs to Meet Every Developer’s Needs # Deliver Dynamic Content Tailored to User Roles, Needs, and Preferences # API documentation transforms into a hyper-personalized resource when it adapts on the fly based on real-time user context. Part of this flexibility is achieved through conditional content delivery, where the documentation site is programmed to render different content based on certain predefined criteria. Essentially, you can create dynamic content layers that automatically tailor the material to each reader’s role, needs, and preferences—whether that means showing backend-specific code samples to certain users or frontend-focused content to others. Implementing this level of personalization requires a fully-equipped documentation platform that effectively categorizes user groups, supports role-specific filtering, navigation, and access controls, and collects helpful analytics data for ongoing optimization. In parallel, building comprehensive profiles for every team role is essential to the effectiveness of dynamic content. Do this by running surveys to gather detailed information on your team members' day-to-day activities. Also, review how different roles have interacted with your documentation in the past and analyze the frequent questions submitted through the portal's search bar. You’ll also need to systematically group your content into logical, well-structured, and separate sections to make navigation easier. Features such as tabs, expandable headings, and clickable blocks will help show or hide information based on varying levels of complexity, projects, and learning objectives. Maximize Localization Impact with Geographical and Industry-Specific Customization # A key strength of hyper-personalized API documentation is how easily it can be customized for different geographies and industries. Making documentation available in local languages has become a standard practice. Yet, technically accurate multilingual translations aren’t enough to make the API fully accessible and useful to every developer around the world. Given the sensitivity of API documentation to region- and industry-specific standards, hyper-customized knowledge libraries include legal guidelines as well as targeted examples , use cases , best practices , and imagery suited to all applicable locations and sectors . For example, they take into account compliance requirements like GDPR in Europe, CCPA in California, and PDPA in Singapore. Although references, developer guides, and training materials are tailored for different contexts across languages, regions, and industries, the core API documentation must always remain consistent. No changes should be made unless there are specific requirements that mandate modifications. Fortunately, present-day documentation systems make managing variations much easier by enabling unified navigation for multiple published knowledge pages. These platforms also natively provide context-aware localization via automated translation, maintain fast load times even with multiple iterations of documentation, include intelligent search filters, and offer version control to track changes across customizations effortlessly. Build Adaptive Documentation Flows for Different User Journeys # Your developers are at different stages in their API documentation journey. Plus, they won’t all have the same level of familiarity with the API. Some developers join the project midway, others are just starting to integrate their first API, while some are already working on complex, large-scale implementations that have urgent deadlines. The same API knowledge can’t be used to serve everyone effectively. Tailor-made API documentation takes into account these diverse experiences. It helps build customized pathways for developers with similar or different profiles , arranged into three distinct tiers: beginner (introduction to basic concepts, step-by-step tutorials with clear instructions, and FAQs), intermediate (advanced tutorials, guidelines for optimizations, and instructions for integrating with third-party tools), and advanced (in-depth API knowledge, strategies for broad-ranging implementations, and live API testing capabilities). The documentation is matched to the user’s current profile, with shortcuts and quick reference guides for experienced developers and more detailed, guided support for newcomers. Frequently accessed sections can be analyzed to further personalize navigation paths through the documentation based on individual behavior patterns. It’s Proven! Real Evidence on How Tailored Experiences Improve Developer Retention # According to Gartner research, teams that benefit from a high-quality developer experience are 20% more inclined to remain with their employer . What’s more, the study confirms that the tools used in daily work routines significantly contribute to this positive experience. As a result, developers are more likely to stay with a company that equips them with the necessary resources for development success. One of these essential tools is hyper-personalized documentation. Documentation directly impacts a developer’s day-to-day work environment. When it’s directly applicable to the projects developers are working on and offers context-specific support, it really improves their workflow efficiency. Developers gain a better understanding of actual work requirements, encounter less friction, and achieve higher success rates with API implementation. Moreover, advanced platforms promote stronger team collaboration by keeping teammates connected both synchronously and asynchronously. All of this results in a more satisfying work experience—which, in turn, leads to lower turnover rates. Introducing Tools That Enable Truly Hyper-Personal API Docs # Explore AI-Driven Insights to Understand User Behavior and Preferences # Analyzing how technical teams interact with AI within documentation portals will reveal extremely valuable user behavior trends. Over time, this data helps refine API documentation to be as accurate as possible and better serve specific user groups. You can also combine AI interaction data with other usage statistics, document feedback, and community talks to spot any meaningful user patterns. Based on recently discovered trends, AI tools will help quickly update documentation by automatically rewriting texts. They’re able to correct spelling errors, improve grammar, and summarize paragraphs whenever necessary. Ultimately, this all-around understanding of user behaviors and preferences lets documentation teams identify the most relevant sections for different developer profiles, prioritize specific topics in future interactions, and deliver content recommendations as granularly as needed. Choose Platforms That Support Real-Time Updates and Modular Content # API knowledge can quickly become outdated. Keeping user-specific materials up-to-date requires a flexible documentation solution capable of immediately reflecting updates or deprecations to existing endpoints and any other vital information. Modern platforms integrate with GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, and other repositories commonly used by technical teams to ensure that API documentation remains automatically synchronized with the latest changes, without disrupting the user experience. Plus, they come equipped with real-time collaboration tools that allow authorized teammates to receive notifications whenever an edit is made, view real-time edits or review the edit history, verify documents for accuracy, and mention each other to provide or respond to feedback. Today’s solutions simplify API documentation maintenance through modular components . These knowledge repositories break down documentation into reusable elements that can be mixed and matched according to user roles. Each block can be adapted and recombined as often as needed. Once you set a variable, you don’t need to manually update the text everywhere. Any changes to the source component will automatically update all related sections to reduce the risk of inconsistencies. Opt for Personalized API Documentation Dashboards # Modern organizations must have the flexibility to adapt their documentation workspace to personal workflows . They need to be able to configure dashboards to display company-wide API documentation, team-level technical resources, project-specific guides, and individual developer materials. Personal dashboards represent the central location where technical staff can efficiently manage their shared and private API-related work . Within this hub, they can track API interactions, access frequently referenced resources, rearrange sections, annotate code in their preferred programming languages, monitor progress on personalized learning paths, and write personal notes. This type of setup will enhance individual and development team productivity. Evaluating the Real-World Impact of Hyper-Personalized API Docs # Companies that adopt a complete documentation platform for hyper-personalized API docs see numerous benefits: 📘 Traject Data (data provider) ➜ after implementing Archbee (a documentation solution that perfectly aligns with their customization needs), Traject Data improved their overall documentation experience. What Does the Future Hold for Hyper-Personal API Docs? # Today, hyper-personal API documentation adjusts itself to the unique roles, workflows, and contexts of each individual developer on your team. This is just the start. As technology evolves, documentation platforms will continuously incorporate innovative features to make the developer experience more engaging, immersive, and… predictive. In the not-too-distant future, documentation will be smart enough to actually predict a developer’s next steps. Using machine learning algorithms, it will anticipate in real time what information resonates most with specific developers before they even start typing their query. Alongside these high-end algorithms for predictive content delivery, the importance of user feedback in API documentation will grow ever more critical. After all, documentation remains relevant only when it effectively serves users—and this is best achieved by continually iterating based on their input. title: The best LeadIQ alternatives in 2026
summary: The best LeadIQ alternatives in 2026, compared on data quality, capture workflow, pricing, and how much of the outbound job each tool actually runs.
body_text: The best LeadIQ alternative for most teams is Artisan, because it does more than capture contacts into a sequencer. It sources leads from a database of over 250M B2B professionals, enriches them, and then runs the email, social media, and dialer outreach itself. LeadIQ speeds up prospecting; Artisan removes most of the job around it. LeadIQ built its following on a tight capture workflow: find a prospect, pull verified contact data, and push it into your CRM and sequencer in a few clicks. For sales development representatives (SDRs) who build lists by hand, this flow is fast. But it is still a data-capture layer on top of tools you buy separately, and that is exactly where the strongest alternatives pull ahead, either on data depth or by owning the outreach entirely. How the best LeadIQ alternatives compare Rank Tool Best for Standout capability Public pricing 1 Artisan Capture plus an AI that runs outreach Autonomous AI BDR across over 250M B2B professionals Usage-based credits for Ava's work; dialer seats billed separately; free trial ( see pricing ) 2 Apollo Capture plus sequencing on a budget All-in-one data and cadences Free to $119/user/month 3 ZoomInfo US enterprise data depth GTM Intelligence Platform, WebSights Over $15K/year reported 4 Cognism EMEA compliance and phone data Diamond Data verification ~$15-50K/year reported 5 Clay Custom enrichment workflows Over 150 enrichment providers, Claygent $167-446/month public tiers 6 Seamless.ai Cheap real-time contact search Live web search for emails Free published; paid tiers gated Why do teams look for a LeadIQ alternative? Usually one of three gaps. The first is data breadth, since LeadIQ is strong for point capture but teams outgrow it when they need a larger, better-verified base or intent signals. The second is cost per outcome, because paying for a capture tool plus a separate sequencer plus a dialer adds up while the capture step is only a sliver of the work. The third is execution. LeadIQ hands the contact to your sequencer, but a rep still writes the messaging, works the replies, and books the meeting. As reply rates fall industry-wide, faster capture into the same manual motion stops moving the number. The right replacement depends on which gap hurts. Sometimes it is more or cleaner data. Sometimes it is compliance. Often it is wanting the whole motion handled instead of just the first click. How we chose Four criteria, weighted for a LeadIQ buyer. How much of the outbound job the tool runs after capture. Data and signal depth, including verification quality. Pricing transparency, since stacking capture and execution tools is a common frustration. And deployment fit, from a single SDR to a central revenue operations (RevOps) team. For the wider data landscape, see our guide to the best B2B data providers . What is the best alternative to LeadIQ overall? 1. Artisan: From capture to booked meeting, run by an AI Artisan replaces the capture-into-sequencer workflow with a system that owns the entire motion. Ava, the AI sales agent at its core, works a database of over 250M B2B professionals in over 200 countries, plus Artisan Local Data with over 250M local businesses. Natural-language search, ideal customer profile (ICP) filters, and intent signals like funding rounds, new executive hires, and active hiring do the list-building LeadIQ leaves to you. She enriches with waterfall email and phone data across roughly a dozen providers, charges only on a successful match, and ranks leads by likelihood of converting. For a focused roundup, see the best email and phone number finder tools for sales . Then she does the part LeadIQ leaves to you. Ava writes one-to-one messaging, so two people in the same campaign receive different emails instead of one template with the name and title swapped. She launches email, social media, and dialer sequences timed to each lead's local business hours, qualifies replies against a knowledge base, chases follow-ups, and books meetings with CRM-owner routing. She also runs dozens of message variations and shifts volume toward the ones that convert. You choose the autonomy level: review-and-approve, objections-only, or full autonomy with plain-language escalation rules and a full audit trail. Over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously. Bruno Didier, CEO of CookUnity Business, put it plainly: "Ava runs highly targeted outreach at a scale we could never reach with a human-only team," at roughly a $45 cost per lead across over 100,000 personalized emails. Native Salesforce and HubSpot sync, bidirectional owner mapping, and field-level export control make it fit a real RevOps stack, beyond a single rep's browser. Best for: teams from startup to enterprise that want the capture-to-meeting motion in one system Who should pick something else: a team that only wants a fast capture button on top of tools it is committed to keeping Pricing: usage-based credits for Ava's work, so you pay for the work she performs; dialer seats and phone numbers billed separately; free trial ( see pricing ) 2. Apollo: Capture plus sequencing at a low price Apollo is the closest low-cost analog to the LeadIQ flow, because it does capture and sequencing in one tool. It offers over 230M contacts, is used by over 600,000 companies (over 100,000 paying), publishes pricing from free to $119/user/month, and acquired Pocus in March 2026. For an SDR who wants to find a contact and drop them straight into a cadence without a second subscription, it is efficient and affordable. Its AI assists a rep instead of acting autonomously, the model is per-seat, and enterprises tend to treat Apollo as a data layer. But as a direct, cheaper replacement for the capture-and-sequence habit, it is the obvious first look. For closer looks, see Artisan vs. Apollo and Apollo vs. Lusha . Best for: SMB and mid-market SDR teams that want capture and cadences in one affordable tool Who should pick something else: teams that want an AI to own replies and booking, or that need enterprise governance Pricing: free to $119/user/month, per its pricing page 3. ZoomInfo: Enterprise data depth If your reason for leaving LeadIQ is data breadth, ZoomInfo is the depth play. Repositioned as a go-to-market intelligence platform and trading as $GTM, it claims over 321M profiles (a marketing figure) and adds WebSights and Scoops. Enterprise teams that need the widest US coverage and an intent layer build around it. It is a data platform first: capture and execution are add-ons, entry contracts are reported at over $15K per year, and its contract terms have a reputation. It is a heavier commitment than a nimble capture tool. For a direct comparison, see ZoomInfo vs. LeadIQ . Best for: enterprises that need the deepest US data and will build execution around it Who should pick something else: small teams that want speed and simplicity, or anyone who wants the outreach run for them Pricing: over $15K per year reported, gated 4. Cognism: Compliance-first EMEA data Cognism is the alternative when your capture problem is really a compliance problem, especially in Europe. Diamond Data phone verification, do-not-call (DNC) and Telephone Preference Service (TPS) scrubbing, and GDPR-aligned processing make it the EMEA data leader. Reps obtain verified mobile numbers they can actually dial. Pricing is gated and reported at roughly $15-50K per year, and it is a data provider, so you still need the sequencer and dialer. Its Kaspr subsidiary was also fined 240,000 euros by France's data protection regulator, the CNIL, in December 2024, per the regulator, which is worth weighing in diligence. Best for: EMEA-focused SDR teams that need compliant, verified phone data Who should pick something else: US-centric teams, or anyone who wants execution bundled in Pricing: roughly $15-50K/year reported, gated 5. Clay: Build your own capture and enrichment Clay is for teams whose capture needs are too custom for a fixed tool. It orchestrates over 150 enrichment providers with Claygent agents, publishes tiers from $167 to $446 per month, and hit a $3.1B valuation in August 2025. You can design a capture-and-enrichment waterfall exactly how you want it. That power is also the cost: Clay is infrastructure that needs a skilled operator, often a go-to-market (GTM) engineer around $160K a year, and median contracts land near $30K. It gives you the workbench; you supply the worker. For a direct comparison, see Artisan vs. Clay . Best for: RevOps and GTM engineers who want fully custom capture and enrichment Who should pick something else: SDR teams that want a fast, ready-made capture flow out of the box Pricing: $167-446/month public tiers; median contracts around $30K/year 6. Seamless.ai: Cheap real-time search Seamless.ai is the budget real-time option, searching the web live to assemble contact data on demand. For price-sensitive teams that want a lot of lookups cheaply, it is tempting as a LeadIQ substitute. The caveats are documented. Reviewers report bounce rates in the 20-30% range, which forces re-verification. Its plans renew annually on auto-renew terms that users report as hard to exit, and in March 2025 it faced reported removal of its company page from a major professional network over scraping. Weigh data quality against the low headline price. Best for: very price-sensitive teams that want high-volume real-time lookups Who should pick something else: teams that need reliable deliverability or clean contract terms Pricing: only a Free plan is published; Pro and Enterprise are gated, on annual auto-renewal terms What is the best enterprise alternative to LeadIQ? Enterprises rarely stop at capture. The two serious paths are ZoomInfo, if the mandate is the deepest data to feed an existing execution stack, and Artisan, if the mandate is fewer tools and more pipeline per head. Artisan carries the enterprise essentials LeadIQ never aimed at: central-ops deployment where sales ops runs Ava for large account executive (AE) teams who never log in, SOC 2 Type II attestation, GDPR and CCPA compliance, single sign-on (SSO), SAML, role-based access, and a full audit trail, with costs that track the work performed instead of headcount. When the enterprise goal is consolidating a stack of five to eight tools instead of adding another capture layer, Artisan is the pick. Stay with LeadIQ if... LeadIQ is the right tool to keep in a few cases. Stay if your SDRs live in a sequencer and CRM you are committed to, and the one thing you need is faster, cleaner capture into them. Stay if your volumes are modest and a lightweight per-seat capture tool is cheaper than a platform. And stay if your data needs are US-centric and mid-depth, where LeadIQ is comfortable. The case to switch strengthens when you are paying for capture plus a sequencer plus a dialer, when reply rates make the manual motion around capture the real bottleneck, or when you want an AI to run the whole thing. title: ¿Qué es una Persona Moral?
summary: Una persona moral es una entidad legal creada por una o más personas físicas o morales, con el fin de realizar actividades económicas, sociales o culturales. A diferencia de una persona física, la persona moral posee derechos y obligaciones independientes de los de sus socios o accionistas y actúa a través de representantes legalmente designados.
body_text: Una Guía de Personas Morales para Product Managers e Ingenieros en México En el dinámico mundo empresarial, los product managers e ingenieros se encuentran constantemente ante el desafío de desarrollar productos y servicios que satisfagan las necesidades tanto de individuos como de empresas. Sin embargo, trabajar con personas morales implica comprender conceptos legales y operativos que pueden ser complejos pero cruciales para el éxito. Este blog post tiene como objetivo desglosar qué es una persona moral, por qué es importante en el desarrollo de productos y cómo nuestras soluciones pueden facilitar su validación y gestión. ¿Qué es una Persona Moral? Una persona moral es una entidad legal creada por una o más personas físicas o morales, con el fin de realizar actividades económicas, sociales o culturales. A diferencia de una persona física, la persona moral posee derechos y obligaciones independientes de los de sus socios o accionistas y actúa a través de representantes legalmente designados. Tipos de Personas Asociadas a la Persona Moral: Representantes Legales: Autorizados para actuar en nombre de la empresa. Órgano de Administración: Dirige y gestiona la empresa. Órgano de Vigilancia: Supervisa el cumplimiento legal y estatutario. Accionistas y Propietarios Reales: Dueños de la empresa que aportan capital y ejercen control. Diferencias entre Persona Moral y Persona Física Para entender plenamente el alcance y las implicaciones de las personas morales, es fundamental distinguirlas de las personas físicas. Persona Física Definición: Un individuo humano con capacidad para adquirir derechos y obligaciones. Responsabilidad Legal: Responde con su patrimonio personal. Ámbito de Actuación: Puede realizar actividades comerciales, pero está limitada en términos de escala y responsabilidades. Persona Moral Definición: Entidad legal con personalidad jurídica propia, independiente de sus miembros. Responsabilidad Legal: Su responsabilidad está limitada al capital aportado; los socios generalmente no responden con su patrimonio personal. Ámbito de Actuación: Puede emprender proyectos de mayor envergadura y tiene acceso a financiamiento y contratos que podrían no estar disponibles para personas físicas. Tipos de Personas Asociadas a la Persona Moral Las personas morales están conformadas por distintas figuras clave que son esenciales para su funcionamiento y cumplimiento legal. A continuación, se detallan los principales tipos de personas asociadas: Representantes Legales Los representantes legales son las personas autorizadas para actuar en nombre de la empresa. Sus responsabilidades incluyen: Firmar contratos y acuerdos: Tienen la facultad de celebrar contratos en representación de la empresa. Toma de decisiones legales y administrativas: Actúan en procesos judiciales y administrativos en nombre de la entidad. Representación ante autoridades y terceros: Son la cara legal de la empresa ante instituciones gubernamentales y socios comerciales. Es fundamental verificar los poderes otorgados a los representantes legales para asegurar que cuentan con las facultades necesarias. Lee sobre los representantes legales de una empresa. Órgano de Administración El órgano de administración es responsable de la dirección y gestión estratégica de la empresa. Dependiendo del tipo de sociedad, puede estar conformado por: Consejo de Administración: Grupo colegiado de individuos que toman decisiones de alto nivel. Administrador Único: Una sola persona encargada de las funciones administrativas. Sus funciones principales incluyen: Definir estrategias y políticas corporativas. Supervisar las operaciones diarias. Tomar decisiones financieras y de inversión. Órgano de Vigilancia El órgano de vigilancia tiene como objetivo supervisar y controlar las actividades del órgano de administración para garantizar el cumplimiento legal y la correcta gestión de la empresa. Generalmente se compone de: Comisarios: Encargados de revisar los estados financieros y operaciones. Auditores Internos: Monitorean los procesos internos y la adherencia a políticas y regulaciones. Sus responsabilidades son: Realizar auditorías y evaluaciones periódicas. Informar a los accionistas sobre irregularidades. Asegurar la transparencia y confiabilidad de la información financiera. Accionistas y Propietarios Reales Los accionistas son los propietarios de la empresa que han invertido capital en ella. Pueden ser personas físicas o morales y tienen derechos proporcionales a su participación accionaria, tales como: Derecho a voto en las asambleas generales. Participación en las utilidades y dividendos. Decidir sobre cambios en la estructura de la empresa. Los propietarios reales son las personas físicas que, directa o indirectamente, poseen o controlan un porcentaje significativo de las acciones o derechos de voto de la empresa, o que ejercen control efectivo sobre ella. Identificar a los propietarios reales es crucial para: Cumplir con regulaciones de prevención de lavado de dinero y financiamiento al terrorismo. Garantizar la transparencia en la estructura de propiedad. Evaluar riesgos asociados con la reputación y cumplimiento normativo. Lee sobre los lineamientos para el conocimiento de propietarios reales. Importancia de Conocer a estas Figuras Para product managers e ingenieros , comprender quiénes son y qué funciones desempeñan estas personas asociadas es esencial para: Diseñar procesos de onboarding eficientes: Adaptando los requisitos y verificaciones según el rol de cada individuo. Cumplir con regulaciones legales: Asegurando que todas las interacciones con la empresa sean conformes a la legislación vigente. Personalizar soluciones y servicios: Entendiendo las necesidades y responsabilidades de cada figura para ofrecer propuestas de valor adecuadas. Oportunidades y Retos en el B2B Trabajar con personas morales ofrece oportunidades significativas, pero también presenta desafíos únicos que los product managers e ingenieros deben considerar. Generación de Más Ingresos Volumen de Compra Mayor: Las empresas suelen realizar compras de mayor volumen y valor. Relaciones Comerciales a Largo Plazo: Contratos y acuerdos que pueden extenderse por años. Onboarding de Empresas Procesos de Validación Rigurosos: Requieren verificación exhaustiva de documentos y cumplimiento regulatorio. Integración Tecnológica: Necesidad de sistemas que puedan manejar información compleja y extensa. Lee nuestra guía sobre el onboarding de empresas. Riesgos Asociados a Empresas Riesgos Legales y Regulatorios: Mayor exposición a sanciones si no se cumple con normativas específicas. Complejidad Operativa: Estructuras organizacionales más complejas que demandan soluciones personalizadas. Necesidades de Clientes Empresariales Soluciones Personalizadas: Requieren productos adaptados a sus procesos y estructuras. Soporte y Servicio al Cliente Dedicado: Expectativas más altas en términos de soporte técnico y atención al cliente. Mayor Retención en B2B que en B2C Fidelidad Comercial: Las empresas tienden a mantener relaciones comerciales estables. Costos de Cambio Altos: La inversión en capacitación y adaptación a nuevos proveedores incentiva la retención. Implicación Práctica: Para capitalizar las oportunidades que presentan las personas morales, es esencial adaptar el desarrollo de productos y servicios a sus necesidades y desafíos específicos. Regulaciones y Cumplimiento Normativo al tener Empresas El entorno legal para las personas morales es más complejo y estricto, lo que exige un mayor nivel de atención y recursos dedicados al cumplimiento normativo. Prevención de Lavado de Dinero (PLD) Obligación Legal: Las empresas deben implementar medidas para prevenir operaciones con recursos de procedencia ilícita. Debida Diligencia: Identificar y verificar la identidad de clientes y beneficiarios reales. Propietarios Reales Transparencia Corporativa: Es necesario conocer a los individuos que en última instancia poseen o controlan la empresa. Registros Actualizados: Mantener información actualizada sobre cambios en la estructura accionaria. Mayor Carga de Análisis de Documentos Documentación Extensa: Actas constitutivas, poderes notariales, estados financieros, entre otros. Análisis Detallado: Verificación minuciosa para asegurar la autenticidad y vigencia de los documentos. Monitoreo de Accionistas y Cambios de Apoderados Actualización Continua: Las empresas pueden cambiar su estructura interna, lo que requiere un seguimiento constante. Riesgo de Incumplimiento: No actualizar esta información puede llevar a sanciones y riesgos legales. Desafío para Product Managers e Ingenieros: Deben asegurar que sus productos y sistemas puedan manejar esta complejidad regulatoria sin comprometer la eficiencia operativa. Lee sobre qué es un representante legal de una empresa. Nuestra Solución para la Validación de Personas Morales Conscientes de estos desafíos, hemos desarrollado una solución integral que facilita y agiliza la validación de personas morales. 1. Extracción de Información de Documentos Tecnología OCR Avanzada: Captura y digitaliza datos de actas constitutivas , poderes notariales y otros documentos clave. Precisión y Velocidad: Reduce errores humanos y acelera el tiempo de procesamiento. 2. Consulta en Fuentes Oficiales Integración con Registros Públicos: Acceso directo al Registro Público del Comercio y otras bases de datos oficiales. Verificación en Tiempo Real: Asegura que la información esté actualizada y sea confiable. 3. Reconciliación y Generación de Informes Análisis Automatizado: Combina y compara datos de múltiples fuentes para detectar inconsistencias. Informes Detallados: Proporciona un panorama completo de la empresa y sus representantes legales y accionistas. Beneficios Clave Tiempos de Análisis Reducidos: Procesos automatizados que aceleran el onboarding. Precisión en los Datos: Minimiza errores y garantiza cumplimiento regulatorio. Facilidad de Integración: API y herramientas que se adaptan a tus sistemas existentes. Conclusión Entender qué es una persona moral y cómo interactuar eficazmente con ellas es esencial para cualquier product manager o ingeniero en México. Si bien presentan desafíos únicos en términos de onboarding, regulación y gestión de riesgos, también ofrecen oportunidades significativas para el crecimiento y la retención a largo plazo. Nuestra solución está diseñada para abordar directamente estos desafíos, proporcionando herramientas que simplifican la validación, aseguran el cumplimiento normativo y permiten a tu empresa enfocarse en lo que realmente importa: innovar y crecer. ¿Listo para optimizar tu proceso de onboarding y gestión de personas morales? body_text: View All News Primo Brands Announces Leadership Changes to Sharpen Focus on Growth Priorities and Customer Experience 07/07/2026 Download (opens in new window) TAMPA, Fla. and STAMFORD, Conn. , July 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Primo Brands Corporation (NYSE: PRMB) ("Primo Brands" or the "Company"), a leading North American branded beverage company focused on healthy hydration, today announced organizational leadership changes designed to strengthen its customer experience, accelerate key growth priorities, and create a more agile, accountable operating model. "As we continue to build Primo Brands, we are moving beyond integration and transformation and into the disciplined work of running and building the business for the future," said Eric Foss, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Primo Brands Corporation. "To deliver on the investment thesis behind the merger, our operating model can and will be fit to win — with a stronger customer focus, deeper go-to-market capability to improve service and execution, and clear accountability and ownership in the parts of the business closest to our customers and frontline associates." As part of these changes, Vaughn Dickinson has joined the Company as President of Customer Direct & Go-to-Market, reporting to the Chief Executive Officer. His experience with multiple fast-moving consumer goods companies, including key leadership roles at PepsiCo, makes him a strong fit for the position as the Company focuses on improving customer experience, service reliability, profitable execution, and route-to-market scalability. As the Company moves to this more streamlined leadership model, the role of Chief Operating Officer will be eliminated. To support a successful transition, Robert Austin will remain with the Company until December 31, 2026. "With the Direct Delivery channel on pace to return to modest comparable growth in the second half of the year, now is the right time to simplify our leadership structure and position the overall business for its next phase of optimization," Foss continued. "We are grateful to Rob for his contributions to the business and will work closely with him to support a smooth and seamless transition." "We anticipate that these changes will create a more agile, accountable operating model centered on our customers and frontline execution. By giving leaders closest to our priorities direct enterprise visibility, we believe we will be better positioned to act with urgency and to deliver more consistently for customers, associates, consumers, stockholders, and the communities we serve." About Primo Brands Corporation Primo Brands is a leading North American branded beverage company focused on healthy hydration, delivering responsibly sourced diversified offerings across products, formats, channels, price points, and consumer occasions, distributed in every U.S. state and Canada. Primo Brands has a comprehensive portfolio of highly recognizable and conveniently packaged branded water and beverages that reach consumers whenever, wherever, and however they hydrate through distribution across retail outlets, away from home such as hotels and hospitals, and food service accounts, as well as direct delivery to homes and businesses. These brands include established "billion-dollar brands" Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and The Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain®, Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified water brands including Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash Refresher™ and AC+ION®. Primo Brands also has an industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers, which create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases. Primo Brands operates a vertically integrated coast-to-coast network that distributes its brands to more than 200,000 retail outlets, as well as directly reaching consumers through its Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill offerings. Through Direct Delivery, Primo Brands delivers responsibly sourced hydration solutions direct to home and business customers. Through its Exchange business, consumers can visit approximately 26,500 retail locations and purchase a pre-filled, multi-serve bottle of water that can be exchanged after use for a discount on the next purchase. Through its Refill business, consumers have the option to refill empty multi-use bottles at approximately 23,500 self-service refill stations. Primo Brands also offers water filtration units for home and business customers across North America. For more information, please visit www.primobrands.com . title: Korn Ferry CEO & Board Survey 2026: Ready or Not
summary: Amid high CEO turnover and AI shifts, boards are under a series of pressures. Can they keep up?
body_text: Same Risks, Different Confidence Agreement on risk doesn’t mean agreement on readiness. Boards and CEOs largely agree on the risks organizations face in 2026 and beyond. But there's a divide in how confident they feel managing them. Across nearly every category tied to transformation and future workforce change, boards reported lower confidence levels than CEOs. Confidence in managing future talent needs Half of all CEOs surveyed are confident their organization can manage future talent and skills challenges. Boards are less confident, suggesting they see greater talent and skills challenges ahead. Respondents confident in their organization's ability to manage talent and skills risk, by respondent group Boards and CEOs approach transformation risk from different positions. CEOs are often closer to execution pressure and operational urgency. Boards are balancing continuity, governance exposure, and longer-term organizational resilience. The confidence gap even shapes how boards and CEOs assess the organization itself. Those different perspectives may also influence succession decisions. Same challenges, but different perspectives CEOs tend to view the organizations they inherit more positively than boards do, suggesting leadership transitions often begin with different assumptions about the challenge ahead. Respondents who rated their organization's operating performance positively, by respondent group Playing It Safe Can Be Risky Looking back on their most recent CEO appointment, 50% of boards say they played it too safe, falling back on what’s worked before instead of what may transform the company now. When the need for agility is high, avoiding risk in succession decisions may carry risks of its own. “Boards are nervous, but leaders feel ready for the challenge.” Jane Edison Stevenson, global vice chair, Board & CEO Services, Korn Ferry Differences in confidence shape how quickly organizations move and how much risk boards are willing to support during periods of transition.
